outcome: Configuration risk and runtime container threats are visible and triaged from one console instead of two.
overview: A fintech running containerised workloads has two different visibility problems, and they need different answers: configuration risk across cloud accounts, which agentless assessment covers well and cheaply, and what a workload is actually doing at runtime, which agentless assessment cannot see at all. Falcon Cloud Security covers both, using agentless connectors for breadth and the same sensor already on the endpoint estate for runtime depth. The design decision worth making deliberately is where each applies, because putting agents everywhere is expensive and putting none anywhere leaves the runtime half blind.

benefits.text: Agentless assessment gives configuration coverage across accounts quickly
benefits.limits: Agentless assessment sees configuration and vulnerabilities, not runtime behaviour; treating it as complete coverage is the usual mistake

benefits.text: Runtime protection uses the same sensor already deployed on the endpoint estate
benefits.limits: Container runtime coverage depends on the orchestration platform and node operating system; the matrix should be checked before scoping

benefits.text: Cloud and endpoint detections appear in one place rather than two consoles
benefits.limits: The platform is agent-and-cloud, so telemetry leaves the customer estate; the tenant region is a design decision to be made and recorded rather than a default to be accepted

residency: Cloud and workload telemetry is processed in the vendor tenant in a selected region, recorded at design

notFor.situation: An estate already running another cloud-native application protection platform
notFor.why: Two platforms produce two finding sets and reconciling them costs more than either resolves

notFor.situation: An organisation with no endpoint deployment of the same platform
notFor.why: The consolidation argument that makes this attractive does not apply
